title: Action laws for the direct sum of twisted sections
statement: Let k be a field, S=k[x_0,x_1] with its total-degree grading and P=Proj S [def-sc-p1-standard]. For an arbitrary O_P-module G and an integer z, put B_z=(PLift(0≤z) → Gamma(P,G tensor O_P(z))), where PLift is the lift of a proposition to a type. Thus B_z is the section group if z≥0 and zero if z<0. Put D=⊕_z B_z. For homogeneous a∈S_e and s∈B_z, define H(e,z,a,s)∈B_(z+e) by h↦(G tensor twistMul(z,a))_*(s) if z≥0 and zero otherwise; the twists and maps are those of [def-weil-pbc-proj-twisting-sheaf]. Define a⋅x for arbitrary a∈S and x∈D to be the finite sum, over nonzero homogeneous components a_e of a and nonzero components x_z of x, of the injection of H(e,z,a_e,x_z) in degree z+e. This explicitly defined operation satisfies 1⋅x=x, (ab)⋅x=a⋅(b⋅x), a⋅(x+y)=a⋅x+a⋅y, (a+b)⋅x=a⋅x+b⋅x. Moreover, for every e≥0, z∈Z, homogeneous a∈S_e and s∈B_z, a⋅ι_z(s)=ι_(z+e)(H(e,z,a,s)).

source.place: Stacks Project, Lemma 01YS(5) (https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01YS), the graded module M_k; Definition 01MN for twists and Lemma 01M7 for localization descriptions and functoriality. Online source read; local text absent.

proof.text: On twists, multiplication by 1/1 is identity and successive multiplication by b/1 and a/1 is multiplication by (ab)/1. Prove the equalities pointwise in Localization.AtPrime, with an eqToHom degree transport. Tensoring by G and taking sections preserve these equalities. The two private coherence lemmas are fully proved.

The homogeneous operation is additive in its section argument. It is additive in its polynomial argument because twistMul is additive, and tensorLeft G is additive: it is a left adjoint in the closed monoidal category of sheaves of modules and hence preserves binary coproducts and biproducts. Zero maps and negative source degrees are handled explicitly.

Bundle the homogeneous bilinear maps into nested DFinsupp.sumAddHom maps and precompose with DirectSum.decomposeAddEquiv. Show by expanding sumAddHom that its value is precisely the given finite double sum. Both distributive laws and both zero laws follow from map_add and map_zero. For a homogeneous scalar and a single summand, apply decompose_of_mem and sum_single_index twice to obtain the single-summand formula, including zero cases.

Induct on the section direct sum for the unit law. For associativity, use DirectSum.Decomposition.inductionOn for each polynomial and DirectSum.induction_on for sections. The additive cases use the proved distributive laws. The homogeneous single-summand case uses the proved section-map composition identity and the degree equality z+(e+f)=(z+f)+e. Negative source degrees yield zero maps. Combine the five proved laws into the original conjunction.

lean.statement:
theorem serreSectionActionLaws :
    (∀ x : serreSectionSum k G, (1 : MvPolynomial (Fin 2) k) • x = x) ∧
    (∀ (a b : MvPolynomial (Fin 2) k) (x : serreSectionSum k G),
      (a * b) • x = a • (b • x)) ∧
    (∀ (a : MvPolynomial (Fin 2) k) (x y : serreSectionSum k G),
      a • (x + y) = a • x + a • y) ∧
    (∀ (a b : MvPolynomial (Fin 2) k) (x : serreSectionSum k G),
      (a + b) • x = a • x + b • x) ∧
    (∀ (e : ℕ) (z : ℤ) (a : MvPolynomial (Fin 2) k)
      (ha : a ∈ MvPolynomial.homogeneousSubmodule (Fin 2) k e)
      (s : serreSectionPiece k G z),
      a • DirectSum.of (serreSectionPiece k G) z s =
        DirectSum.of (serreSectionPiece k G) (z + e)
          (serreSectionHomogeneous k G e z ⟨a, ha⟩ s))
